title: What does an architect do before a building goes up?
answer: An architect turns ideas about a building into plans other people can build from. Imagine a school that needs a new room for music. The architect asks who will use it and what needs to fit inside. The plans show where the walls, doors, and windows go and how people move between rooms. The architect also works with other people, such as engineers, who check whether the parts can carry the loads they will face.

title: What do civil engineers make possible?
answer: Civil engineers plan structures and systems that whole communities use. A road project might need a path that follows the land, a way for rain to drain, and enough room for people to cross. A bridge project might need supports that can carry both the bridge and the people using it. Other civil engineers work on water systems. The work starts before a crew begins building and can continue long after a project opens.

title: How does a land surveyor measure a place?
answer: A land surveyor measures the positions of points on the ground. Pretend a path is going to cross a hill where no street signs mark the way. The surveyor can record where important features sit and how high they are. Those measurements help a designer know how far apart things are before drawing a plan. Surveyors also look at earlier records when they work out the location of a property boundary.

title: What do mapmakers choose to show?
answer: A mapmaker collects information about places and decides which details a map should show. A map for a park visitor might mark trails and restrooms. A map for a bus rider might skip most trails and make bus stops easy to spot. Mapmakers can use measurements from the ground and pictures taken from above. They choose labels and symbols to make the map readable, then change it when the information needs updating.

title: Who designs the outdoor parts of a park?
answer: A landscape architect plans outdoor places such as parks, plazas, and schoolyards. The job can include deciding where paths go, which parts stay open for play, and where trees can give shade. The designer also thinks about water after rain and how people with different ways of moving can reach the same places. A good plan joins the parts together so they can work as one outdoor space.

answer: A building inspector visits construction projects to check how the work matches rules meant for buildings. An inspector may look at a particular kind of work, such as wiring or plumbing. Some checks happen while parts are still open and easy to see. If the work needs a change, an inspector can tell the builder which part needs attention. For example, a door that fits its opening must still have room to move. The carpenter checks the size of the opening and how straight its sides are.

answer: A roofer installs or repairs the covering at the top of a building. A roof can meet a wall, a pipe, or a skylight, so the job includes working around changes in shape. answer: An auto mechanic checks how a car or light truck is working and repairs or replaces parts when needed. answer: One address shows where a letter is meant to go. A return address tells postal workers where it came from. That matters when people send mail across a country where some street names are used in many towns.
facts: A postal address can include a person’s name, street, city, and ZIP Code.

title: Why does a little stamp help a letter travel?
answer: A postage stamp shows that part or all of the cost of sending a piece of mail has been paid. Think of it as a small label showing that the letter has paid for its trip through the mail system. Stamps can also carry pictures, so two that serve the same purpose can look very different. A postal service can show postage in other ways too, such as a paid label on a package.
facts: The first U.S. postage stamps, issued in 1847, showed Benjamin Franklin and George Washington.

title: How can a postcard travel without an envelope?
aliases: why postcards do not need envelopes
answer: A postcard is a stiff card that can carry a message through the mail without an envelope around it. One side may have a picture. The other can hold a note and the details the mail service needs to know where to deliver it. A postcard’s message can be seen by someone handling the card. The size and shape matter because pieces of mail have to pass through different kinds of equipment.
facts: Picture postcards and cards sold with postage already printed on them are both part of U.S. postal history.

title: How can machines sort so many letters by address?
answer: In a mail processing center, machines can send letters with different destinations along different paths. A printed barcode can carry information about where a piece should go. After reading the code, a machine can put that letter with other pieces headed toward the same area. Some mail needs other kinds of handling, such as pieces that do not fit the machines. Later, mail can be grouped for the routes used by local carriers.
facts: A barcode read by sorting equipment can give it destination information without the machine reading each part of a written address on every pass.

title: How does a tracking page know where a package has been?
answer: A package that can be tracked has a number that connects it to a set of records. Machines or workers can scan its label at different stops. The service records things such as arrival at a facility, and those records can show up on the tracking page. The package can spend time traveling between scans. In that case, the most recent update tells you where something was recorded, rather than showing its position moving along a road.
facts: A tracking page can have information before the first trip if the sender has already provided the service with a label record.

title: How do snowplows make a path along a street?
answer: A snowplow uses a wide blade to push snow out of a travel path. Moving the snow creates a clearer path for the next vehicle, but the snow is still somewhere nearby. A crew might make several passes if the street is wide or more snow keeps falling. When a city has many streets, crews follow plans that can give some routes early attention, such as roads that serve important buildings.
facts: In some cities, trucks carry extra snow away when there is not enough room to keep it beside a street.

title: How can a small crack in a road turn into a pothole?
answer: A pothole can start where the road surface or the material underneath has become weak. Water can get through a crack and soften the layers beneath the road. In some weather, freezing and thawing can make the damage worse. As traffic passes, pieces of the weakened surface can loosen and break away. A hole can then grow as more tires hit its edges. Crews can fill the hole and may also need to work on its cause.
facts: Potholes can also form in places where water rarely freezes.

title: Why do roads have both yellow and white lines?
answer: Painted lines on a road help people understand how the space is divided. In the United States, a yellow center marking can show where lanes for opposite directions meet. White lines often divide lanes going the same way. Other marks can show where a road edge is or where a crossing begins. The markings work together with signs and lights to give people clues about a place even before they reach it.
facts: A road can have different kinds of markings close together because they show different parts of the road.

title: Why does a truck brush dirt off the street?
answer: Loose leaves, grit, and bits of litter build up on streets. A street sweeper can move along the road gathering some of that material. Brushes on some sweepers pull it toward the part of the machine that collects it. Sweeping can also keep some dirt out of storm drains, where rain would have carried it. Where cars are parked close together, the sweeper may have trouble reaching the edge of the street.
facts: Cleaning along the curb can matter because loose material often collects at the edge of a road.

title: Why do crews check bridges that people already use?
answer: A bridge inspector looks at the condition of a bridge after it has been built. Parts that were new when it opened can change over time. Inspectors can look for things such as damaged pieces or changes in the surface and record what they find. Some important parts are underneath rather than next to the road. The records help people decide which work a bridge needs and what later inspections should pay attention to.
facts: A bridge inspection can involve looking at the parts that support the deck as well as the deck itself.

title: Why do many streets have a fire hydrant?
answer: A fire hydrant gives firefighters a place to get water from a supply below or beside the street. In many towns it connects to the same network of water mains that sends water toward buildings. Its connections let a crew bring that water into its equipment at an emergency. Hydrants can be spread across the area a water system serves. The shape above the sidewalk is just one visible part of the system.
facts: The pipe called a water main carries water for a number of places, rather than for just one faucet.

title: How does a water meter know how much water a building used?
answer: A water meter measures the amount of water passing along a pipe. When someone uses a sink or a shower, water can pass through the building’s meter on its way there. The reading keeps a running total. Comparing two readings shows how much water passed in the time between them. A reading from last week and a reading from today can tell a different story from either number alone.
facts: Water meters may show amounts in units such as gallons or cubic feet.

title: What does an electricity meter count?
answer: An electricity meter measures how much electrical energy goes into a building. The reading can grow more quickly when many things use electricity at once or when something that uses a lot of power runs. A common unit on a bill is the kilowatt-hour. That is the energy used by one kilowatt of power running for an hour. A meter keeps adding to its count as time passes.
facts: Power describes how fast energy is being used. The meter counts the amount used over time.

title: How can used water go uphill inside a sewer?
answer: Many sewers let used water flow downhill through pipes. A route cannot always keep going down, because the treatment plant or the next useful pipe may be higher than the low point the water has reached. A lift station can collect water there and pump it to a higher place. From that point, the water can go downhill again where the pipe allows it. Several parts of the trip may work differently.
facts: A pipe that carries pumped water under pressure is sometimes called a force main.

title: How can natural gas reach a place far from where it was found?
answer: Natural gas can travel inside long pipelines to areas far from its source. Systems serving towns then use other pipes to bring gas closer to the places that use it. The line going to one building can be much smaller than the lines that move gas across a region. Some places use gas for heat or to power equipment. Gas and drinking water move through different networks of pipes.
facts: Long-distance transmission pipelines and smaller local distribution pipes do different parts of the work.

title: Why do public buses stop at certain places along a route?
answer: A public bus can follow a route that links neighborhoods and places people want to visit. Instead of stopping everywhere, it has a set of places where riders can usually get on or off. Shared stops help a route serve many people while keeping the trip moving. A schedule can list when a bus is expected to reach particular stops. Actual arrivals can change when traffic or the number of riders changes.

title: How can people borrow a city bicycle for one trip?
answer: A bike share system makes bicycles available for trips by many different people. In a system with docks, a rider takes a bicycle from a station and can return it to a different station after the trip. Once it is back, someone else can use it. Stations may be placed near parks, neighborhoods, or other kinds of transport. It helps to have a way to see where bicycles and empty docks are available.
facts: Some bike share systems use docks, and others use marked parking areas or a different way to end a trip.

title: What happens around an airplane between flights?
answer: After a plane reaches its gate, other workers get it ready for its next trip. Some workers move luggage between the airplane and the equipment that takes it to another part of the airport. A crew can also bring supplies and check that the plane’s space on the ground is clear for the next step. The teams share the area and have to do jobs in a useful order. facts: People working near a parked airplane are often described as a ground crew or ramp crew.

The station can combine the loads of several trucks onto a larger vehicle for the longer trip. Collection crews can then go back to their routes. Not every place uses a transfer station, and the destination depends on the local system.

title: How can a landfill hold rubbish in one place?
answer: A landfill is a planned place where waste is put for long-term disposal. At many modern sites, workers build sections for rubbish and use barriers to help keep liquids from moving into nearby ground. As one area fills, the waste can be covered and later loads can go to another area. People looking after the site can monitor what happens to water and gas. A landfill takes up land because the rubbish stays there.
facts: Rain and other liquids can pick up material from waste as they move through it.

title: What happens to a mixed bin of recycling after pickup?
answer: A recycling sorting center separates useful materials that arrive together. The work often starts with a moving belt carrying items past machines or workers. Paper, plastic, metals, and glass may need to go in different directions because each can be made into different things. A center may press some sorted material into dense bundles before it travels onward. Different communities collect different materials, so the mix arriving at a center can vary.
facts: Sorting and making a new product are usually separate steps, and they can happen at different sites.

title: How can old paper turn into new paper?
answer: Paper is made from a mat of tiny fibers pressed together. At a paper mill, old paper can be mixed with water so the fibers separate. The mill can remove things that should not be in the new paper. Then the wet fibers can be spread again, pressed, and dried into a sheet. Some old fibers break into pieces that are too short to keep using, which can limit how many times paper is recycled.
facts: Recycled fibers can be mixed with other fibers to make products that need different strengths.

title: How can an old aluminum can help make new metal products?
answer: An aluminum can can become useful metal again after it has been collected and sorted. At a processing plant, old aluminum can be cleaned and melted. The melted metal can then be shaped into a larger piece that a factory can use. A maker may roll material into sheets for cans or use it for another product. An old can need not keep its shape for the metal in it to be useful.
facts: A new can may contain metal from many old objects, mixed together before being made into sheet.

title: Where can an old computer or phone go after someone stops using it?
answer: A device that still works may be repaired or passed along for someone else to use. facts: A device contains many kinds of material in a small space, which is one reason it is sorted differently from a single aluminum can.

title: Why do products often stop in a warehouse before reaching a store?

answer: A warehouse can gather things that come from different factories or farms. Workers record what has arrived and where it is stored. Later, one store might need paper towels while another needs boxes of cereal. The warehouse can put together the right load for each place instead of making each producer send a separate truck to every store. A distribution center often moves goods onward as part of that job.

title: Why do workers stack boxes on a pallet?
answer: A pallet is a low platform that holds goods together while they are stored or moved. Several boxes can sit on one pallet instead of traveling as separate loads. Spaces beneath the platform leave room for the lifting parts of special equipment to slide under it. Workers can then move the stack as one group. Pallets often help when goods go from a warehouse into a truck or need to be moved again at the other end.

title: How can frozen food stay cold from a factory to a store?

answer: Frozen food may travel through several places before a shopper sees it. It can spend time in a cold part of a factory, travel in a vehicle that can cool its load, and wait in refrigerated storage before reaching a store. This chain of cool places and trips is called a cold chain. The people arranging the trip have to think about transfers as well as the time spent traveling.
facts: Cold storage means goods can wait between trips without being stored in an ordinary warm room.

title: What makes a farmers market different from a regular grocery store?
answer: At a farmers market, several sellers usually bring food and other goods to one place, often on certain days. Some of the sellers are people who grew or made what they sell. answer: A freight train can carry many loads between places linked by railroad tracks. A truck can reach roads and buildings well beyond those tracks. answer: A retail business sells things to people who will use them. A wholesale business usually sells to other businesses or organizations. title: Why does a shop count things even if nobody is buying them yet?
answer: A shop’s inventory is the set of goods it has on hand, or a record of those goods. A shop needs to know which items are ready to sell and which need replacing. answer: A receipt records a purchase. It may list the date, the things bought, and a total.
